title: The Signal of Station Meridian
premise: Sebastian Coldharbour, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs supply routes between worlds that severed contact decades ago. When the ship Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember a massacre no record confirms, Sebastian becomes their reluctant guardian and investigator. The station's ruling Consortium has rewritten history to hide that it sold the colony's air, water, and lives; as the station reactor counts down toward an 'emergency reset' that will erase the last physical evidence, Sebastian and the child-crew must recover buried memory cores and broadcast the truth. In the end, justice arrives outside any court: the truth is transmitted to every world at once, the Consortium falls to its own frightened citizens, and Sebastian plants the garden's first seed in soil that finally belongs to someone.
about_author: E. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote environmental monitoring stations before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about ordinary people keeping systems alive inside institutions designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He pilots his hauler between silent worlds, tending seed vaults for colonists who may never come. Establishes loneliness, duty, and the strange peace of gardening for ghosts. Beat: quiet melancholy interrupted by an anomalous distress ping from deep space.

chapters.title: What Came Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian docks at Station Meridian to find a ship returned after forty years missing—crewed by children wearing adult uniforms. POV shifts between Sebastian and Wren, the youngest 'returned' officer. Beat: uncanny dread mixed with tenderness.

chapters.title: Children in Uniform
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The de-aged crew remembers a voyage of decades compressed into years of body. Wren recalls fire, screaming, and a sealed door—but Station officials call it trauma-induced confabulation. Beat: gaslighting begins.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Welcome
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Administrator Voss greets the Meridian with staged celebration and quiet confiscation of the crew's logs. Sebastian notices records being purged in real time. Beat: polite menace beneath ceremony.

chapters.title: A Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Sebastian tends the terraforming bay, his only sanctuary. Wren wanders in, drawn by green things she shouldn't remember loving. Their friendship forms over seedlings. Beat: fragile warmth.

chapters.title: The First Denial
chapters.summary: Wren testifies before a Consortium tribunal about the massacre at Colony Halcyon; her testimony is dismissed as childhood fantasy. Sebastian watches her break. Beat: injustice crystallizes.

chapters.title: Countdown Discovered
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A maintenance friend reveals the reactor is on a scheduled 'historical data purge'—a countdown that will wipe archival cores in thirty days. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Halcyon Was Real
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, dreamlike. Fragmented memories surface: a colony begging for air filters, a vote to let them die, the order to forget. Beat: grief and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Allies in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sebastian recruits Okafor, a disgraced station archivist, and Tam, a reactor tech with doubts. Small conspiracy forms in the garden bay. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: The Purge Begins Early
chapters.summary: Voss accelerates deletions; Okafor loses half her archive overnight. The group realizes they're being watched. Beat: paranoia tightens.

chapters.title: Stowaway Logic
chapters.summary: Wren sneaks aboard Sebastian's hauler to reach Halcyon's ruins herself. Sebastian catches her—and decides to go with her rather than turn her in. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Crossing the Silence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV en route. Worlds that stopped speaking pass by like closed mouths; he tells Wren why the routes died. Beat: worldbuilding through sorrow.

chapters.title: Ash Orchard
chapters.summary: They land at Halcyon: a dead colony preserved like a museum no one visits. Wren walks rooms she remembers burning. Beat: haunted recognition.

chapters.title: The Sealed Door
chapters.summary: In Halcyon's sublevel, the door from Wren's memories—welded shut from outside. Inside: remains and a black-box memory core. Beat: horror confirmed physically.

chapters.title: Evidence That Isn't
chapters.summary: Okafor radios: the core's checksum won't match official records; the Consortium pre-emptively registered 'forged' versions. Truth alone won't be enough. Beat: despair.

chapters.title: Witnesses Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Revelation chapter: the de-aging wasn't accident but punishment—a Consortium experiment to erase testimony by erasing the witnesses' credibility and eventually their memories entirely. Beat: thematic core lands.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Child
chapters.summary: Back at Meridian, Voss gently interviews Wren while Sebastian listens hidden, learning Voss was the officer who gave the burn order. Beat: villain humanized and damned.

chapters.title: The Garden Sabotaged
chapters.summary: Someone torches Sebastian's terraforming bay—the one place that was safe. He understands: they'll take everything he tends. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Pressured to trigger the purge early, he stalls, then defects with reactor schematics showing a manual override window. Beat: courage of small people.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Days
chapters.summary: Planning chapter. The team maps the archive vaults, the broadcast array, and the countdown. Sebastian proposes the unthinkable: seize the array and transmit everything. Beat: the plan takes shape.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under stress, her adult memories flood back fully—including the name of every person who died at Halcyon. She recites them as an act of witness. Beat: mourning as resistance.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: One of the child-crew betrays the plan to Voss, hoping to be restored to adulthood. The trap is set. Beat: betrayal and pity.

chapters.title: Arrest at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Sebastian is seized mid-loading; the memory core confiscated. Okafor and Wren escape into the station's underlevels. Beat: darkest hour opens.

chapters.title: The Undercity of Meridian
chapters.summary: Wren and Okafor find generations of people erased from station records living in maintenance warrens—people with no legal existence. Natural allies. Beat: solidarity discovered.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV in detention. Voss offers him the garden, funding, a future—if he surrenders the children and calls it mercy. Sebastian refuses. Beat: temptation declined.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Coolant Lines
chapters.summary: Tam engineers Sebastian's release during a reactor inspection. Tense traversal of the station's guts. Beat: kinetic relief.

chapters.title: The Second Core
chapters.summary: Okafor reveals a backup: Halcyon's sister colony kept mirrored archives, stored in the derelict Meridian itself. The evidence is on the ghost ship all along. Beat: reversal of hope.

chapters.title: Boarding the Ghost Ship
chapters.summary: Sebastian, Wren, and Tam board the aged-backward Meridian, walking corridors where the massacre's orders were given. Beat: confrontation with history's furniture.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Is Eight
chapters.summary: They find the Meridian's captain, now a child, who hid one final core inside a toy. Her testimony names Voss directly. Beat: innocence carrying unbearable weight.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days
chapters.summary: Race montage: copying cores, dodging patrols, the countdown accelerating as Voss panics. Beat: rising tempo.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Voss seals the station, cutting the undercity off. The erased people rise anyway, opening doors with stolen codes. Beat: the forgotten become the many.

chapters.title: Broadcast Array Assault
chapters.summary: The team fights toward the transmission tower; Tam holds the reactor override while Sebastian and Wren climb. Beat: action climax begins.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Voss confronts them atop the array, offering the official version one last time: there was no massacre, only logistics. Wren answers with the names. Beat: moral duel.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Sebastian broadcasts everything—cores, testimony, the sealed-door footage—to every world on the long route. The silence between worlds breaks as replies flood in. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Three Minutes to Reset
chapters.summary: Voss triggers the purge manually. Tam's override fails partially; the reactor countdown becomes real. Evacuation chaos. Beat: physical peril peak.

chapters.title: The Garden Holds
chapters.summary: Sebastian reroutes coolant through the terraforming bay, saving the station by sacrificing the garden he built. Beat: costly sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Fall
chapters.summary: Voss arrested not by law but by the crowd of people she erased; the Consortium dissolves. Justice rendered outside courts, imperfectly, together. Beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Children
chapters.summary: The de-aged crew speaks publicly; the station chooses to believe children over its own archives. Some begin experimental restoration; Wren declines, choosing to grow forward. Beat: bittersweet grace.

chapters.title: New Routes
chapters.summary: Worlds reopen contact; ships move again along the long route. Sebastian is offered command of the new charter and declines—he wants his hands in soil, not ledgers. Beat: return to self.

chapters.title: First Seed
chapters.summary: Sebastian plants the garden's first seed in rebuilt soil, Wren beside him naming the beds after Halcyon's dead. Memory kept not in records but in living things. Beat: resolution and renewal.
